newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal rebels kill five soldiers in India ambush.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels kill five soldiers in India ambush.

text.p: Separatist tribal guerrillas ambushed a security patrol in the northeastern Indian state of Assam, killing at least five Indian paramilitary soldiers and wounding five, police said on Tuesday.
They said Naga guerrillas opened fire on the patrol when it was passing through the mountainous North Cachar Hill district late on Monday.
The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland in Nagaland state, adjacent to Assam. No other details were immediately available.
India's northeastern region, comprising seven states rich in minerals and timber with more than 200 ethnic groups, has been rocked by separatist violence for decades.
The hilly, heavily forested region is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and linked to the rest of India by a 20-km (12-mile) wide corridor in the eastern state of West Bengal.
